label: Dream Incubation
description: Ancient Egyptian and Greek practice of sleeping in temples to receive prophetic dreams

label: Aboriginal Dreamtime
description: Australian Aboriginal cosmology where dreams connect to ancestral creation and ongoing spiritual reality

label: Biblical Dream Interpretation
description: Dreams as divine messages requiring interpretation
importance: seen in Hebrew and early Christian texts

label: Artemidorus
description: Author of Oneirocritica
importance: one of the earliest systematic dream interpretation manuals

label: Sigmund Freud
description: Founder of psychoanalysis; proposed dreams as disguised fulfillment of unconscious wishes

label: Wish Fulfillment
description: Freud's theory that dreams express repressed desires in symbolic form

label: Manifest vs Latent Content
description: Freud's distinction between a dream's surface story and its hidden true meaning

label: The Unconscious Mind
description: The reservoir of repressed thoughts and desires theorized to drive dream content

label: Dream-Work
description: Freud's term for the mental processes that disguise latent content into manifest imagery

label: Carl Jung
description: Former Freud collaborator who broke away to found analytical psychology

label: Collective Unconscious
description: Jung's theory of shared ancestral memory and symbolism underlying all human minds

label: Archetypes
description: Jung's universal symbolic figures (Shadow
column7: Self) recurring across dreams and myths

label: Individuation
description: Jung's process of psychological integration

label: Alfred Adler
description: Broke from Freud to found individual psychology
importance: viewing dreams as tied to compensation for felt inferiority

label: Compensation Theory
description: Adler's idea that dreams help the psyche work through feelings of inferiority

label: Calvin Hall
description: Developed the cognitive theory of dreams and a system for content-analyzing dream reports

label: Cognitive Theory of Dreams
description: Views dreams as reflections of a dreamer's everyday concerns and conceptions of self and others

label: Hobson and McCarley
description: Neuroscientists who proposed the activation-synthesis model

label: Activation-Synthesis Model
description: Theory that dreams arise from the brain synthesizing meaning from random brainstem activity during REM

label: REM Sleep
description: Rapid Eye Movement sleep stage discovered to correlate strongly with vivid dreaming

label: Neurocognitive-Biological School
description: Approach explaining dreams primarily through brain physiology rather than symbolic meaning

label: Antti Revonsuo
description: Proposed the threat simulation theory as an evolutionary explanation for dreaming

label: Threat Simulation Theory
description: Evolutionary theory that dreaming rehearses threat perception and avoidance for survival

label: Evolutionary School
description: Framework explaining dreaming as an adaptive trait shaped by natural selection

label: Memory Consolidation Theory
description: Theory that dreaming helps process and consolidate memories and learning from waking life

label: William Domhoff
description: Continued Hall's content-analysis approach and critiqued purely biological dream theories

label: Rosalind Cartwright
description: Researched dreams' role in emotional regulation and mood processing

label: Emotional Regulation Theory
description: Theory that dreaming helps process and regulate emotional experiences from waking life

label: Lucid Dreaming
description: State of being aware one is dreaming while still asleep

label: Stephen LaBerge
description: Pioneered scientific research and induction techniques for lucid dreaming

label: Psychoanalytic School
description: Broad tradition treating dreams as windows into unconscious conflict and desire

label: Analytical Psychology
description: Jungian tradition treating dreams as sources of symbolic and archetypal meaning

label: Surrealist Art
description: Art movement led by Dali and Breton directly inspired by Freudian dream theory

label: Modern Psychotherapy
description: Continued clinical use of dream interpretation in various forms of talk therapy

label: Film and Dream Logic
description: Cinema's use of dream sequences and non-linear dream logic

label: Pop Psychology and Dream Dictionaries
description: Popularized
importance: often oversimplified dream symbol interpretation for mass audiences

label: Dream Journaling Apps
description: Modern digital tools for recording and pattern-analyzing personal dreams

label: Sleep Science and Neuroscience
description: Academic and clinical field studying sleep architecture and dream physiology
